# /dev on a Linux ground station: the top level and /dev/serial/by-id, the only two directories
# Mission Planner globs, each in readdir order. devtmpfs lists newest first, so the devices plugged
# in last lead and ttyACM1 precedes ttyACM0. Hand-made, modelled on a real machine: a Pixhawk 6X
# running ArduPilot (two CDC interfaces), an FTDI FT232R adapter, a paired Bluetooth radio, and the
# nodes every PC has. Serial numbers are invented.
#
# Entry lines: an absolute path; a directory ends in "/"; a symlink shows " -> target".
# usb| lines: what the serialport crate reports for a device node - node|vid:pid|serial|manufacturer|product.
/dev/rfcomm0
/dev/ttyACM1
/dev/ttyACM0
/dev/hidraw2
/dev/ttyUSB0
/dev/serial/
/dev/usbmon2
/dev/usbmon1
/dev/usbmon0
/dev/vboxusb/
/dev/usb/
/dev/hidraw0
/dev/pts/
/dev/bus/
/dev/ttyprintk
/dev/ttyS3
/dev/ttyS2
/dev/ttyS1
/dev/ttyS0
/dev/ptmx
/dev/tty2
/dev/tty1
/dev/tty0
/dev/console
/dev/tty
/dev/urandom
/dev/random
/dev/zero
/dev/null
/dev/serial/by-id/usb-ArduPilot_Pixhawk6X_3A0045001351333031383238-if00 -> ../../ttyACM0
/dev/serial/by-id/usb-ArduPilot_Pixhawk6X_3A0045001351333031383238-if02 -> ../../ttyACM1
